title: P02/P45-family handoff: halve every residual-stream write (emb, attention proj, fc2) after pretraining, a function-preserving rescale
description: P02 follow-up (handoff transform, same family as P45/P46): after the unchanged 070-claude pretraining, multiply emb.weight and every block's proj and fc2 weights and biases by 0.5; every residual write is read back only through a LayerNorm (ln1/ln2/ln_f), so the handed-off function is unchanged up to LayerNorm eps (logit drift is measured and logged). This isolates the plasticity mechanism proposed for the 1x/3x/10x Muon weight-decay trend (316/327/353): the frozen RL AdamW takes roughly fixed-size per-element steps, so halving these weights doubles their relative RL step size without the pretraining-quality and sampling-time costs that broke 30x decay (071).
hypothesis: Higher Muon weight decay helped expert iteration because smaller weights let the fixed-LR RL AdamW move the policy further per round (plasticity), not because the decay improved the pretrained function. A function-preserving halving of the residual-stream writers (whose scale is invisible to the forward pass because every read is LayerNormed) doubles their effective RL learning rate relative to weight size while keeping val loss, held-out greedy and round-1 sampling identical to 070. If plasticity is the mechanism, RL rounds 2-4 should solve more targets and dev-transfer >=7 rises; if the decay trend worked through the function itself (e.g. softer logits from a smaller head, which this does not touch), this is a no-op or hurts via RL instability. Residual readers (qkv, fc1, head, LayerNorms) are untouched.
expected_delta: -40 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central guess +0); pretraining identical to 070 (same steps, val loss, held-out greedy); handoff logit drift < 1e-2

arch.change: none versus 070-claude during pretraining; at handoff the residual-stream writers are rescaled (see handoff), architecture and parameter count unchanged
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 069-claude except Muon weight decay)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1 on all 21 Muon matrices (peak per-step shrinkage 1e-3); AdamW auxiliary wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: CHANGED: after the pretraining loop and model.eval(), under no_grad, multiply by RESID_SCALE=0.5: emb.weight (99x256), and in each of the 5 blocks proj.weight, proj.bias, fc2.weight, fc2.bias (21 tensors). Every residual write is read only through ln1/ln2/ln_f (LayerNorm, eps 1e-5), so logits change only through eps; the max |logit| difference on the first 128 val records (fp32, no autocast) is logged and returned as stats.handoff_logit_drift (local CPU check on a random-init fork GPT(99,5,256,8) with a 10x-scaled embedding: 4.5e-4 at logit scale 1.4). Not rescaled: qkv, fc1, head, LayerNorm gains/biases. Pretraining optimizer states are discarded and the frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW (lr per harness, wd 0.1, betas 0.9/0.95, clip 1.0), whose ~lr-sized per-element steps are then ~2x larger relative to the rescaled weights.

config.init: Exactly 070-claude (= 069-claude): fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude.
